significance.basis: Delivers a clean, zero-float exact-Q verification harness and explicit worked benchmarks (including the L=3 4-line central fan DAG and N=4..16 Fig. 2 truncations) validating Dury [3] on concrete instances, though general multi-dimensional proofs remain unformalized.

potential_errors: Mode 4 checks a 3-tuple potential proxy (lambda, dim F, S) which is exact only for r <= 2; on the r = 3 octant certificate (#16) this suffices only because all 7 targets jump immediately to lambda = infinity, and for Certificate #10 (d=3, dim F=0, r=3) Table 2 displays only a single scalar S^F transition 0 -> 1 rather than the full (r-1)-component slice vector.

Sec. 1 'Explicit non-claims' lists Theorems 1-8 and 13-18 when summarizing the algebraic projections, omitting Theorems 9-12 (the Figure 2 counterexample laws) from that sentence even though they are included in Table 1.

Claims regarding 0-sorry/0-warning Lean compilation, 0.110-1.003 ms replay latencies, and 66/66 adversarial test rejections depend on external repository artifacts that cannot be executed or independently audited from the PDF alone.
strengths: Transparent scope calibration: Section 1 ('Honest Two-Layer Scope Calibration' and 'Explicit non-claims') clearly delineates what is universally proved in Lean 4 vs. checked on finite exact-Q witnesses vs. left to Dury [3].

Complete algebraic and KKT consistency: Every theorem in Table 1 holds mathematically, the Figure 2 identities (p_k in H_k cap H_{k-1}, envelope step, y_0 in [-1, 0), and 2^{-N} gaps) are exact, and all sign vectors, strict-complementarity KKT duals, flag layers, and DAG edges in the 8-chamber 4-line central fan (Sec. 4, Fig. 2(a)) check out exactly.

Consistent numerical reporting across text, tables, and figures: Axiom counts (5 none, 1 propext, 12 [propext, Quot.sound]), replay latencies (0.110-1.003 ms across 16 certificates), and red-team counts (12+13+12+14+15 = 66/66) align throughout.
summary: This 4-page companion paper presents a two-layer formal and exact-rational verification stack for Brennan Dury's objective-driven acyclic chamber digraph framework [3]. Layer 1 is a standalone 18-theorem Lean 4.35.0 kernel (HyperplaneTraversal.lean, 0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice) proving single-coordinate sign-closure poset axioms, sign-flip counting/distinctness properties, cleared integer laws for Section 2 Figure 2's quasipolyhedral non-attainment counterexample, and scalar/3-tuple algebraic projections of Frame slice and DAG bounds. Layer 2 is a pure-Python zero-floating-point exact-Q verifier (ARRANGEMENT-TRAVERSAL-CERT-1.0) checking 16 canonical certificates across four modes (Theorem 2 flag targets up to d=4, r=4; Figure 2 truncations up to N=16; Frame slices; and KKT chamber DAGs including an explicit 8-chamber 4-line central fan with L=3) and rejecting 66/66 adversarial forgeries. All visible algebraic identities, KKT witnesses, sign vectors, axiom tallies, and cross-table statistics in the PDF are internally consistent and accurately scoped, with no unresolved material objections.
weaknesses: Elementary mathematical depth of the Lean 4 kernel: Many of the 18 theorems in Table 1 are single-line integer/natural-number arithmetic identities or basic enum case analyses (e.g., #5, #7, #8, #9, #10, #12, #13, #15, #16, #17, #18), while general d-dimensional arrangement geometry, LP duality, compactness, and graph acyclicity remain unformalized.

Small scale of finite certificates: The Mode 4 DAG atlas covers low-dimensional instances (d <= 4, at most 9 chambers in 2D and 8 in 3D) and relies on a 3-tuple potential proxy (exact only for r <= 2) rather than the general (r+1)-component potential P*_F.
Figure 2(b) merely plots the linear tautology L_max = k - 1 and L = L_max + 1 = k across k = 1..8, offering minimal empirical or analytical value beyond the one-line bound in the text.
